items.title: Yes Boone Signs With Warner, Progresses on Debut Album
items.summary: Newly signed to Warner Music, rising artist Yes Boone is progressing on a debut album blending French house and post-punk influences.

items.title: Noisia Reunite After Seven-Year Hiatus
items.summary: Dutch electronic trio Noisia is reuniting after seven years apart, with their first show back together set for Amsterdam in December.

items.title: BMG Deepens Jean-Michel Jarre Partnership
items.summary: BMG has deepened its partnership with electronic music pioneer Jean-Michel Jarre, securing exclusive worldwide licensing rights to his recorded catalog.

items.title: Porridge Radio's Dana Margolin Launches Debut Solo Single
items.summary: Porridge Radio frontperson Dana Margolin has released a debut solo single following the band's breakup last year.

items.title: Believe France Launches ALL IN Pop Entity
items.summary: Believe France launched ALL IN, a new pop label entity uniting several existing imprints under managing director Henri Jamet.

items.title: DICE Owner Fever Raises $250M at $5.2B Valuation
items.summary: Fever, owner of ticketing platform DICE, raised $250 million led by EQT at a $5.2 billion valuation, its largest funding round yet.

items.title: Universal and Warner Press Court on Udio, Suno Musicians' Lawsuit
items.summary: Universal and Warner are pushing courts to dismiss a musicians' lawsuit over their licensing deals with AI music generators Udio and Suno.

items.summary: Music publishers allege Anthropic purchased and destroyed physical songbooks after scanning them, and are now seeking to identify which songs were copied.

items.summary: Believe and TuneCore say they will not supply artists' music to AI platform Suno without explicit opt-in consent from rights holders.

items.title: BMI Launches Free Healthcare Service for Songwriters
items.summary: Performing rights organization BMI launched a free service helping US songwriters and composers navigate and find healthcare coverage options.

items.summary: Songwriter Cyril Vetter is urging the Supreme Court to reject majors' and BMG's challenge to a ruling letting songwriters reclaim copyrights.
